title: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context
abstract: arXiv:2610.23246v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model's input, from multi-agent debate, where agents read their peers' responses, to self-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts. In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent's output becomes another's input. We study the regime where token reading and generation draw on one fixed token window, so every token spent reading is a token that cannot be spent reasoning. We develop a \textbf{token-budget theory} that formalizes this trade-off, modeling accuracy as a function of the reasoning budget remaining after reading and aggregating votes with a Condorcet jury model that permits correlated errors. For multi-agent debate, the theory gives a closed-form prediction for the optimal number of agents. This quantity is estimated from single-agent measurements, allowing the optimal group size to be determined without running deb

translated_title: 多思考还是多阅读？共享上下文下推理的Token预算理论
translated_abstract: 推理系统越来越多地通过在模型输入中纳入额外上下文来改进答案，从多智能体辩论（智能体阅读同伴的回答）到自我改进（模型重新审视自己的草稿）皆是如此。在这些系统中，通信会消耗上下文，因为一个智能体的输出会成为另一个智能体的输入。我们研究了token阅读与token生成共享同一固定token窗口的情形，因此每花费一个token用于阅读，就少一个token可用于推理。我们提出了一个**token预算理论**来形式化这种权衡，将准确率建模为阅读后剩余推理预算的函数，并采用允许错误相关的Condorcet陪审团模型来聚合投票。对于多智能体辩论，该理论给出了最优智能体数量的闭式预测。这一数量可从单智能体的测量中估计得出，从而无需实际运行辩论即可确定最优群体规模。
tldr: 提出token预算理论形式化固定上下文窗口下“阅读他人输出”与“自主推理”的权衡，通过允许错误相关的Condorcet陪审团模型推导出多智能体辩论最优智能体数量的闭式解，且仅需单智能体测量即可估计最优群体规模。
en_tdlr: Proposes a token-budget theory formalizing the trade-off between reading others' outputs and reasoning within a fixed context window, deriving a closed-form prediction for the optimal number of agents in multi-agent debate that can be estimated from single-agent measurements alone.
